text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000212 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity tier, including many low-complexity visits, but the small set of returned charts mostly supports the billed level, so the picture is mixed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation is not confined to sicker patients: 99215 share runs above the all-provider rate even for patients with zero chronic conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215s include many single, apparently minor diagnoses, such as rash (R21) on C0100810, C0100858 and C0101161 and an upper respiratory infection (J06.9) on C0100325, which fits a pattern consistent with upcoding. Against that, the 18 documented 99215 claims show an unsupported rate well below the comparison providers, with high-MDM support on claims like C0101090 and C0101192. However, records cover only about 3% of claims, and the note checks cut the other way: some notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim (e.g., C0100271), and C0101161 is both a low-complexity 99215 and a note flagged for problems. That makes cloned or inflated documentation a possibility, though not proof. A reviewer should first request charts targeted at the low-complexity 99215 claims listed here and an EHR audit trail to check whether those notes were templated."}
